metadata.title: Improved Approximation Algorithms for Maximum Cut and Satisfiability Problems Using Semidefinite Programming
metadata.authors: Michel X. Goemans, David P. Williamson
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: MAX CUT problem
nodes.statement: Given undirected graph $G=(V,E)$ with nonnegative edge weights $w_{ij}=w_{ji}$, find $S \subseteq V$ that maximizes $w(S,\bar{S}) = \sum_{i \in S, j \in \bar{S}} w_{ij}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Find a vertex subset $S$ that maximizes the total weight of edges crossing between $S$ and its complement.

nodes.name: MAX 2SAT problem
nodes.statement: Given a collection $\mathcal{C}$ of Boolean clauses, each of length at most 2, with nonnegative weights $w_j$, find an assignment of truth values that maximizes the total weight of satisfied clauses.

nodes.name: MAX SAT problem
nodes.statement: Given a collection $\mathcal{C}$ of weighted Boolean clauses (any length), find an assignment maximizing total weight of satisfied clauses.

nodes.name: MAX DICUT problem
nodes.statement: Given a directed graph $G=(V,A)$ with arc weights $w_{ij}$, find $S \subseteq V$ maximizing the weight of arcs with tail in $S$ and head in $\bar{S}$.

nodes.name: MAX RES CUT problem
nodes.statement: Variant of MAX CUT where pairs of vertices in $E^+$ must lie on the same side and pairs in $E^-$ on different sides of the cut.

nodes.name: $p$-approximation algorithm
nodes.statement: A polynomial-time algorithm that delivers a solution of value at least $p$ times the optimal value (for randomized variants, expected value at least $p \cdot \mathrm{OPT}$). The constant $p$ is the performance guarantee.

nodes.name: Semidefinite program
nodes.statement: Optimization of a linear function of a symmetric matrix $Y$ subject to linear equality constraints and the constraint that $Y$ is positive semidefinite.

nodes.name: Positive semidefinite matrix
nodes.statement: An $n \times n$ symmetric matrix $A$ such that $x^T A x \geq 0$ for every $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$. Equivalent: all eigenvalues nonnegative; or $A = B^T B$ for some matrix $B$.

nodes.name: Gram matrix
nodes.statement: For unit vectors $u_1,\ldots,u_n \in S_n$, the matrix $Y$ with $y_{ij}=u_i \cdot u_j$. Any positive semidefinite $Y$ with $y_{ii}=1$ corresponds to such a set of unit vectors via $Y=B^T B$.

nodes.name: Laplacian matrix
nodes.statement: For a weighted graph, $L=(l_{ij})$ defined by $l_{ij}=-w_{ij}$ for $i \neq j$ and $l_{ii}=\sum_k w_{ik}$.

nodes.name: Correcting vector
nodes.statement: A vector $u \in \mathbb{R}^n$ satisfying $\sum_{i=1}^n u_i = 0$, used in the Delorme-Poljak eigenvalue bound.

nodes.name: Strongly self-dual polytope
nodes.statement: A polytope $P \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ inscribed in the unit sphere, circumscribed around a sphere of radius $r$ ($0<r \leq 1$), with a bijection $\sigma$ between vertices and facets such that facet $\sigma(v)$ is orthogonal to vertex $v$.

nodes.name: Constant $\alpha$ (MAX CUT performance guarantee)
nodes.statement: $\alpha = \min_{0 < \theta \leq \pi} \frac{2}{\pi} \cdot \frac{\theta}{1-\cos\theta} > 0.87856$, achieved at $\theta=2.331122\ldots$, the nonzero root of $\cos\theta + \theta\sin\theta = 1$.

nodes.name: Constant $\beta$ (MAX DICUT performance guarantee)
nodes.statement: $\beta = \min_{0 \leq \theta \leq \arccos(-1/3)} \frac{2}{\pi} \cdot \frac{2\theta - \pi}{1 + 3\cos\theta} > 0.79607$.

nodes.name: Integer quadratic program (Q) for MAX CUT
nodes.statement: Maximize $\tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{i<j} w_{ij}(1 - y_i y_j)$ subject to $y_i \in \{-1,1\}$ for all $i \in V$. The set $S=\{i : y_i=1\}$ realizes a cut of weight $\tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{i<j} w_{ij}(1-y_i y_j)$.

nodes.name: Vector relaxation (P) of MAX CUT
nodes.statement: Maximize $\tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{i<j} w_{ij}(1 - u_i \cdot u_j)$ subject to $u_i \in S_n$ (unit sphere in $\mathbb{R}^n$) for all $i \in V$.

nodes.name: Semidefinite program (SD) for MAX CUT
nodes.statement: Maximize $\tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{i<j} w_{ij}(1-y_{ij})$ subject to $y_{ii}=1$ and $Y=(y_{ij})$ symmetric positive semidefinite.

nodes.name: Dual semidefinite program (D)
nodes.statement: Minimize $\tfrac{1}{4}\sum_i \gamma_i + \tfrac{1}{4}\sum_{i<j} w_{ij}$ subject to $W + \mathrm{diag}(\gamma)$ positive semidefinite.

nodes.name: Goemans-Williamson MAX CUT algorithm
nodes.statement: Randomized $(\alpha-\epsilon)$-approximation: solve the SDP relaxation, then use a uniformly random hyperplane through the origin to partition the vectors.
input: Undirected graph $G=(V,E)$ with nonnegative edge weights $w_{ij}$
output: A cut $(S, \bar{S})$ whose expected weight is at least $(\alpha - \epsilon) \cdot Z_{MC}^*$
nodes.pseudocode: (1) Solve relaxation (P) (via SDP) to obtain optimal unit vectors $u_i$. (2) Draw $r$ uniformly from the unit sphere $S_n$. (3) Set $S = \{i : u_i \cdot r \geq 0\}$.

nodes.name: Solve SDP relaxation
nodes.statement: Solve the relaxation (P), obtaining an optimal set of unit vectors $u_1,\ldots,u_n \in S_n$ (computed via the equivalent SDP up to additive error $\epsilon$).

nodes.name: Draw random hyperplane
nodes.statement: Draw $r$ uniformly distributed on the unit sphere $S_n$ (e.g., normalize $n$ i.i.d. standard normals; normalization unnecessary for the sign test).

nodes.name: Hyperplane rounding
nodes.statement: Return $S = \{i : u_i \cdot r \geq 0\}$, partitioning the vectors into those above and below the random hyperplane normal to $r$.

nodes.name: MAX RES CUT algorithm
nodes.statement: Apply the MAX CUT algorithm to relaxation (P) augmented with constraints $u_i \cdot u_j = 1$ for $(i,j) \in E^+$ and $u_i \cdot u_j = -1$ for $(i,j) \in E^-$.

nodes.name: MAX 2SAT algorithm
nodes.statement: Randomized $(\alpha-\epsilon)$-approximation for MAX 2SAT via vector relaxation (P') of (Q'), with hyperplane rounding using auxiliary vector $u_0$ to define truth values.
input: MAX 2SAT instance with weighted clauses of length $\leq 2$

nodes.name: MAX SAT $.7584$-approximation algorithm
nodes.statement: Randomized algorithm picking with probabilities $p_1,p_2,p_3$ among: (1) $x_i$ true with prob $1/2$; (2) $x_i$ true with prob $v(x_i)$ from SDP; (3) hyperplane rounding $\mathrm{sgn}(u_i \cdot r) = \mathrm{sgn}(u_0 \cdot r)$. With $p_1=p_2=.467, p_3=.066$ achieves $.7584$.

nodes.name: MAX DICUT algorithm
nodes.statement: Same hyperplane rounding applied to vector relaxation (P'') of integer quadratic program (Q'') for directed cut, yielding $(\beta-\epsilon)$-approximation with $\beta > 0.79607$.

nodes.name: Expected cut value (Theorem 3.1)
nodes.statement: Given any unit vectors $u_i \in S_n$, the expected weight of the cut produced by the random hyperplane algorithm equals $E[W] = \sum_{i<j} w_{ij} \cdot \frac{\arccos(u_i \cdot u_j)}{\pi}$.

nodes.name: Hyperplane separation probability (Lemma 3.2)
nodes.statement: $\Pr[\mathrm{sgn}(u_i \cdot r) \neq \mathrm{sgn}(u_j \cdot r)] = \frac{1}{\pi}\arccos(u_i \cdot u_j)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.2
nodes.statement: By symmetry, the probability the random hyperplane separates $u_i,u_j$ equals $2\Pr[u_i \cdot r \geq 0, u_j \cdot r < 0]$. The set $\{r: u_i \cdot r \geq 0, u_j \cdot r < 0\}$ is a spherical digon of angle $\theta = \arccos(u_i \cdot u_j)$, so it has measure $\theta/(2\pi)$ of the sphere; result follows.

nodes.name: Performance guarantee (Theorem 3.3)
nodes.statement: $E[W] \geq \alpha \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{i<j} w_{ij}(1 - u_i \cdot u_j)$, where $\alpha = \min_{0<\theta\leq\pi} \frac{2}{\pi}\frac{\theta}{1-\cos\theta}$.

nodes.name: Arccos lower bound (Lemma 3.4)
nodes.statement: For $-1 \leq y \leq 1$, $\frac{1}{\pi}\arccos(y) \geq \alpha \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}(1-y)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.5
nodes.statement: Calculus shows $\alpha$ is achieved at $\theta = 2.331122\ldots$, the nonzero root of $\cos\theta + \theta\sin\theta = 1$. Use concavity of $1-\cos\theta$ on $[\pi/2,\pi]$ to derive $\alpha \geq 2/(\pi \sin\theta_0) > 0.87856$ at $\theta_0=2.331122$.

nodes.name: Refined bound when MAX CUT is large (Theorem 3.1.1)
nodes.statement: Define $A = \frac{1}{W_{\mathrm{tot}}}\sum_{i<j} w_{ij}\frac{1-u_i \cdot u_j}{2}$. If $A \geq \gamma \approx 0.84458$, then $E[W] \geq W_{\mathrm{tot}} \cdot h(A)$ where $h(t) = \arccos(1-2t)/\pi$, giving performance guarantee $h(A)/A - \epsilon$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.1.1
nodes.statement: Set $\lambda_e = w_e/W_{\mathrm{tot}}$, $x_e=(1-u_i \cdot u_j)/2$. Replace $h$ with its largest pointwise-convex minorant $\bar{h}$ (linear of slope $\alpha$ on $[0,\gamma]$, equal to $h$ on $[\gamma,1]$). For $A \geq \gamma$, $\sum \lambda_e h(x_e) \geq \sum \lambda_e \bar{h}(x_e) \geq \bar{h}(\sum \lambda_e x_e) = h(A)$ by Jensen on $\bar{h}$.

nodes.name: Negative weights bound (Theorem 3.2.1)
nodes.statement: Let $W_- = \sum_{i<j} w_{ij}^-$ where $x^- = \min(0,x)$. Then $E[W] - W_- \geq \alpha \left(\tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{i<j} w_{ij}(1-u_i \cdot u_j) - W_-\right)$.

nodes.name: Arccos variant bound (Lemma 3.2.2)
nodes.statement: For $-1 \leq z \leq 1$, $1 - \frac{1}{\pi}\arccos(z) \geq \alpha \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}(1+z)$.

nodes.name: MAX CUT alternative formulation (Theorem 3.3.1)
nodes.statement: $Z_R^* = Z_{MC}^*$, where (R) is the nonlinear program: maximize $\sum_{i<j} w_{ij} \arccos(u_i \cdot u_j)/\pi$ subject to $u_i \in S_n$.
conclusions: Optimum of (R) equals the maximum cut value

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.3.1
nodes.statement: $Z_R^* \geq Z_{MC}^*$ since (R) relaxes (Q) (the objective reduces correctly on $\pm 1$ vectors). Conversely, by Theorem 3.1, given optimal vectors of (R), the random hyperplane algorithm produces a cut of expected value exactly $Z_R^*$, so some realized cut achieves at least this value.

nodes.name: Delorme-Poljak eigenvalue bound (Lemma 4.3.1)
nodes.statement: Let $u \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with $\sum_i u_i = 0$. Then $\frac{n}{4}\lambda_{\max}(L + \mathrm{diag}(u))$ is an upper bound on $Z_{MC}^*$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.3.1
nodes.statement: Let $y$ be optimal for (Q); then $y^T L y = 4 Z_{MC}^*$. By Rayleigh, $\lambda_{\max}(L+\mathrm{diag}(u)) \geq y^T(L+\mathrm{diag}(u))y/(y^Ty) = (1/n)(4Z_{MC}^* + \sum y_i^2 u_i) = 4 Z_{MC}^*/n$ since $y_i^2=1$ and $\sum u_i = 0$.

nodes.name: Eigenvalue minimization (EIG)
nodes.statement: $Z_{EIG}^* = \inf g(u)$ subject to $\sum_i u_i = 0$, where $g(u) = (n/4)\lambda_{\max}(L+\mathrm{diag}(u))$.

nodes.name: Worst-case ratio (Corollary 5.1)
nodes.statement: For any MAX CUT instance, $Z_{MC}^*/Z_P^* \geq \alpha$.

nodes.name: MAX 2SAT performance guarantee (Theorem 7.2.1.1)
nodes.statement: $E[V] \geq \alpha \sum_{i<j}[a_{ij}(1-u_i \cdot u_j) + b_{ij}(1+u_i \cdot u_j)]$, implying $(\alpha-\epsilon)$-approximation for (Q') and MAX 2SAT.

nodes.name: Three-vector same-sign probability (Lemma 7.3.1)
nodes.statement: $\Pr[\mathrm{sgn}(u_i \cdot r) = \mathrm{sgn}(u_j \cdot r) = \mathrm{sgn}(u_k \cdot r)] = 1 - \frac{1}{2\pi}(\arccos(u_i \cdot u_j) + \arccos(u_i \cdot u_k) + \arccos(u_j \cdot u_k))$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.3.1
nodes.statement: Define events $A$ (all sgn equal), $B_i,B_j,B_k$ (one differs), and $C_i,C_j,C_k$ (the pair excluding the index agrees). Use $\Pr[A]+\sum \Pr[B_l]=1$, $\Pr[C_l]=\Pr[A]+\Pr[B_l]$, sum to get $\sum \Pr[C_l] = 1+2\Pr[A]$, then apply Lemma 3.2 to each $\Pr[C_l]$.

nodes.name: Three-vector inequality for MAX DICUT (Lemma 7.3.2)
nodes.statement: For any $u_i,u_j,u_k \in S_n$, $1 - \frac{1}{2\pi}(\arccos(u_i \cdot u_j) + \arccos(u_i \cdot u_k) + \arccos(u_j \cdot u_k)) \geq \frac{\beta}{4}(1 + u_i \cdot u_j + u_i \cdot u_k + u_j \cdot u_k)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.3.2
nodes.statement: Let $a=\arccos(u_i \cdot u_j), b=\arccos(u_i \cdot u_k), c=\arccos(u_j \cdot u_k)$ ranging over the spherical-triangle set $S$. Minimize $h(a,b,c)$ over $S$ via case analysis: boundary cases $a+b+c=2\pi$, $c=a+b$ (and symmetric), zero / $\pi$ cases reduce to interior; interior critical point yields $a=b=c$ giving $h \geq 0$ from definition of $\beta$.

nodes.name: Case 1: $a+b+c = 2\pi$
nodes.statement: Then $1 - (a+b+c)/(2\pi) = 0$ and trigonometric identities give $1+\cos a + \cos b + \cos c = 2\cos((a+b)/2)[\cos((a+b)/2)+\cos((a-b)/2)] \leq 0$, so $h \geq 0$.

nodes.name: Case 2: $c=a+b$ (or symmetric)
nodes.statement: Setting $x=(a+b)/2$, claim reduces to $1 - 2x/\pi \geq (\beta/2)\cos(x)(1+\cos x)$, verifiable as $1 - 2x/\pi \geq (0.81989/2)\cos x(1+\cos x)$ for $0<x<\pi/2$.

nodes.name: Cases 3-4: degenerate boundary
nodes.statement: If $a=0$ then $b=c$ and reduces to Case 2; if $a=\pi$ then $b+c=\pi$ and reduces to Case 1.

nodes.name: Case 5: interior critical point
nodes.statement: Gradient vanishes implies $\sin a=\sin b=\sin c=2/(\beta\pi)$ with $\cos a,\cos b,\cos c \geq 0$, giving $a=b=c$. Then $h(a,a,a) = 1 - 3a/(2\pi) - (\beta/4)(1+3\cos a) \geq 0$ from $a \leq 2\pi/3$ and definition of $\beta$.

nodes.name: MAX SNP-hardness limits
nodes.statement: MAX CUT, MAX 2SAT, MAX DICUT are MAX SNP-hard, so a constant $c<1$ exists such that $c$-approximation implies $P=NP$. Bellare et al. show $c \leq 83/84$ for MAX CUT and $95/96$ for MAX 2SAT.

nodes.name: 5-cycle gap
nodes.statement: For the 5-cycle, $Z_{MC}^*/Z_{EIG}^* = 32/(25+5\sqrt{5}) \approx 0.88445$, very close to $\alpha$, showing the worst-case analysis is nearly tight.

nodes.name: Computational results on random graphs and TSPLIB
nodes.statement: Implementation using Vanderbei's SDP code with 50 random hyperplanes: on random graphs (Types A-D, sizes 50-200), cuts within 4% of SDP bound on average; on 10 TSPLIB instances, optimal cut found in 5 cases, all within 0.5% of bound.

nodes.name: 11-vertex instance with ratio $<.8796$
nodes.statement: Unweighted 11-vertex graph (Figure 2) for which $E[W]/Z_P^* < 0.8796$, with optimum vectors having a 3-dimensional representation; a 103-vertex weighted instance gives ratio $<0.8786$. Based on Lovasz's strongly self-dual polytopes.

nodes.name: Combinatorial $.878$-approximation for MAX CUT
nodes.statement: Can a $0.878$-approximation algorithm for MAX CUT be obtained without explicitly solving the semidefinite program (analogous to primal-dual LP-free vertex cover)?

nodes.name: Tighter SDP relaxations
nodes.statement: Does adding additional constraints to the semidefinite program (e.g., constraints exact for planar graphs) lead to a better worst-case approximation bound for MAX CUT?
